claims.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy declared that Kyiv will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after Moscow targeted Ukrainian infrastructure.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times regarding refinery attacks: 'The block is out. We're done.'
Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that more than 100 civilians had been killed in Russian attacks over the past week.
Ryazan Governor Pavel Malkov stated that Ukrainian drone strikes caused a fire at a refinery owned by Rosneft.
Ukrainian state energy company Naftogaz reported that a Russian strike on a gas production facility east of Kyiv forced operations to halt.
Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine's military was temporarily deprived of US early-warning alerts for incoming ballistic missiles.
Zelenskyy's office confirmed that Starlink satellite functionality was restored and speed restrictions were lifted.
US President Donald Trump denied that Washington had cut off intelligence-sharing with Ukraine.
Romanian President Nicușor Dan reported that two Russian drones struck two chemical tankers in Romanian territorial waters, causing fires.
Ukraine's military used a Neptune cruise missile to strike an airfield in Russia's southern Voronezh region, damaging Sukhoi Su-34 jets.
More than 360 Russian drones targeted Ukraine's central Kirovohrad region, killing three people and injuring six.
Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Kyiv attempted to hit refineries on Wednesday but caused no significant damage.
Italy's Defence Minister Guido Crosetto stated to the BBC that US restrictions on intelligence-sharing with Kyiv would be a 'complete mistake.'
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced during a meeting with Zelenskyy in London that the UK would speed up lightweight multirole missile deliveries to Kyiv.
The Ukrainian Air Force reported stopping 536 Russian drones overnight out of more than 850 launched.
Russia's Defense Ministry reported that Russian air defenses downed 166 Ukrainian drones overnight.
A 16-year-old gunman killed three children and a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon.
Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz stated the attacker forced entry into the school by shooting at locked doors.
A community member pursued the shooter into Silver Rail Elementary School and shot him dead.
The three children killed in the Bend school shooting were aged five, eight, and 11.
A seven-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were hospitalized in critical condition following the shooting.
Police received the first emergency call at 12:59 p.m. local time after a suspect fired a long gun into a car outside the school.
Bend Police spokesperson Sheila Miller reported that two injured victims were transported to St. Charles Bend hospital.
Bend-La Pine School District announced the cancellation of Friday classes, activities, and athletic events across the district.
FBI Director Kash Patel posted on social media that the agency was on scene assisting local law enforcement.
Oregon Governor Tina Kotek publicly thanked the armed bystander who intervened to stop the shooter.
The Gun Violence Archive documented 369 mass shootings in the United States in 2026 as of October 15.
A school rooftop collapse in Peshawar, Pakistan, killed at least 34 children.
Hospital officials reported at least 33 pupils and a teacher were killed in the Peshawar school roof collapse.
Peshawar Police Chief Mian Saeed announced the arrest of the school's owner following the collapse.
The roof collapse occurred at the privately run al-Khair school in Peshawar at 8:48 a.m. local time.
Regional emergency services director Arif Khattak reported that at least 45 children were injured in the disaster.
Lady Reading Hospital spokesperson Mohammad Asim stated the fatalities included 12 girl students and a female teacher.
A total of 110 students were attending lessons in three classrooms when the roof collapsed.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi ordered a formal report into the cause of the roof collapse.
Emergency official Arif Khattak stated that the al-Khair school building had been constructed on a temporary basis.
Governor Faisal Karim Kundi ordered a comprehensive safety audit of all schools across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Houthi forces fired missiles and drones at al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16.
Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani stated Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani and cabinet members were unharmed.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree stated fighters struck the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden.
The UN Security Council issued a joint statement condemning escalatory Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and commercial shipping.
The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a cruise missile over Medina province and destroying drones in Eastern Province and Khamis Mushait.
Yemeni Health Minister Qasim Buhaibeh stated the victims of the Aden attack included security guards and civilian staff.
Saudi Arabia's Deputy Foreign Minister Rayed Krimly accused Iran of encouraging Houthi escalation.
Iran's foreign minister stated Iran is prepared to assist in facilitating talks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.
Yemen's health ministry reported at least 1,282 people killed and 5,890 injured in Yemen fighting since August 6.
Houthi spokesperson Brigade General Yahya Saree denied Houthi involvement in the missile intercepted over Medina.
Emergency teams searched for seven missing crew members after two chemical tankers were attacked in the Black Sea.
Romanian MEP Nicolae Stefanuta stated regarding Black Sea threats: 'It is clear that sooner or later we will have European casualties.'
The San Marino-flagged tanker Wine Trader caught fire 13 nautical miles east of Sulina following reported explosions.
Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed that both the Wine Trader and the Comoros-flagged Yara J were struck by drones.
Russia stated it struck two cargo ships carrying military cargo heading to Ukraine's Odesa port.
Leaders of Romania and Bulgaria prepared to discuss invoking Article 4 of the NATO treaty.
Romanian Defense Minister Radu Miruta stated an investigation was underway into whether the Wine Trader was hit by a drone in Romanian territorial waters.
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced the EU summit would discuss a proposed moratorium on Black Sea attacks on civilian ships.
